crossRefs.note: Saul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Keilah, to besiege David and his men.
He struck Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and nursing babies…
What if there are fifty righteous within the city? Will you consume and not spare the place for the fifty righteous who…
But he scorned the thought of laying hands on Mordecai alone, for they had made known to him Mordecai’s people.…
As a roaring lion or a charging bear, so is a wicked ruler over helpless people.
“Their feet are swift to shed blood.
Destruction and misery are in their ways.

people.name: David
people.line: Anointed king of Israel, ancestor of Jesus Christ

people.name: Israel
people.line: Patriarch, son of Isaac, father of twelve tribes

people.name: Keilah
people.line: A town in the Shephelah of Judah, rescued by David

people.name: Saul
people.line: First king of Israel, anointed by Samuel

translations.web: Then David said, “O Yahweh, the God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
translations.bsb: And David said, “O LORD, God of Israel, Your servant has heard that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the city on my account.
translations.kjv: Then said David, O LORD God of Israel, thy servant hath certainly heard that Saul seeketh to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
translations.asv: Then said David, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, thy servant hath surely heard that Saul seeketh to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
